path: LCG > Beginners guide > Utility buttons explained
title: Skeleton Cut
text: Skeleton Cut Use this when you have cut only a few parts from a full sheet and a lot of sheet is still left. Press Skeleton Cut. Then use the controller to move the laser head to the point where you want to cut, on X or Y. The machine cuts a straight line along X or Y.

path: LCG > Beginners guide > How to cut a program on an offcut
title: Select the program and press EDIT
text: Select the program and press EDIT Highlight the program you want to cut on the offcut. It must turn green. Then press EDIT.

path: LCG > Beginners guide > How to cut a program on an offcut
title: Find the line to change
text: Find the line to change Once you are in the program, find the line marked in red. This line is usually in every LCG and ENSIS program. The default values on it are J2400 and Q1000.

path: LCG > Beginners guide > How to cut a program on an offcut
title: Change J and Q
text: Change J and Q Change J to 200 and Q to 100, so the line reads J200 and Q100. This works perfectly on all programs. Only if the offcut is really tiny, use J50 and Q50.

path: LCG > Beginners guide > How to cut a single part of a full program
title: Select the program and press EDIT
text: Select the program and press EDIT Choose your program and highlight it. It must turn green (1). Then press EDIT (2).

path: LCG > Beginners guide > How to cut a single part of a full program
title: Press G<-DIAGRAM
text: Press G<-DIAGRAM Once you are in the program editor, press G<-DIAGRAM.

path: LCG > Beginners guide > How to cut a single part of a full program
title: Click a hole in your part
text: Click a hole in your part On the drawing, click on any hole of the part you want to cut (2). Click a hole INSIDE the part. Do not click outside the part.

path: LCG > Beginners guide > How to cut a single part of a full program
title: Search for the part number
text: Search for the part number Press SEARCH (1). Type N0 in the box (2). Choose UP (3). Then press SEARCH NEXT (4).

path: LCG > Beginners guide > How to cut a single part of a full program
title: Find the first line of your part
text: Find the first line of your part The search highlights the part number, for example N0007 (1). Look just above it and find the first M104 (2). Remember its line number. In this example it is 2307. This is the first line of your part.

path: LCG > Beginners guide > How to cut a single part of a full program
title: Find the last line of your part
text: Find the last line of your part Now choose DOWN (1) and press SEARCH NEXT (2). It finds the next part number, for example N0008 (3). Look just above it and find the first M104 (4). In this example it is line 2512. This is the last line of your part.

path: LCG > Beginners guide > How to cut a single part of a full program
title: Copy your part
text: Copy your part Close the search box and press COPY. Choose the first line (for example 2307) and the last line (for example 2512) of your part. Then copy it.

path: LCG > Beginners guide > How to cut a single part of a full program
title: Delete the rest of the program
text: Delete the rest of the program Delete everything in the program, so only the lines at the top and the lines at the bottom are left, as in the photo. Put the cursor at the end of the M103A0 line (marked in red).

path: LCG > Beginners guide > How to cut a single part of a full program
title: Paste your part
text: Paste your part Press PASTE (1). Only the part you copied is pasted. The drawing now shows just that one part (2).

path: LCG > Beginners guide > How to cut a single part of a full program
title: Move the part
text: Move the part Copy the line that starts with G93X8.Y12 (this is an example). Paste it under M103A0. Then change the X or Y position to move the part where you want it. Only change the second G93 line. Leave the first one where it is.

title: Example video
text: Example video Watch this video for an example of the whole process.

path: LCG > Machine cleaning
title: Slide out the trays and clean
text: Slide out the trays and clean Slide out the trays from under the machine. Clean off all the scrap and metal dust and hoover it out. Do this every 2-3 days at minimum. Do this EVERY SINGLE TIME after cutting aluminium.

path: LCG > Machine cleaning
title: Open the doors and clean the bed and rails
text: Open the doors and clean the bed and rails Open the main doors. Clean the front of the machine and hoover out all the dust. Also remove the bed from the machine and hoover out all the dust and metal scrap from the rails. Do this EVERY WEEK.

path: LCG > Machine cleaning
title: Empty the dust collector
text: Empty the dust collector Clean the dust collector and empty out the bucket. Put the bucket back in correctly so it does not leak dust. Do this every 3-4 days, and EVERY SINGLE TIME after cutting aluminium. Safety: Wear a safety mask while doing this.

path: LCG > Machine cleaning
title: Open the back doors and hoover out the marked area
text: Open the back doors and hoover out the marked area Open the back doors. Clean and hoover out the marked area (the red square and the rails) to remove all dust and metal scrap.

path: LCG > Cleaning the lens
title: Cleaning the lens
text: Cleaning the lens You will need: acetone, cotton balls and nitrile gloves. Make sure the area around you is clean. Put on nitrile gloves. Remove the lens from its holder. Blow the dust off both sides of the lens. Dip a cotton ball in acetone and gently clean one side of the lens. Take a new cotton ball with no acetone and wipe away all the wet area on that side. Repeat the same two steps on the other side. Blow off both sides once more and check that no dust is left. DO NOT PRESS HARD on the lens while using cotton balls.
